titleText: Inside the thaw that led a pair of New England prep stars to commit to Boston College
mainText: It became a story within the story.Boston College's decision to not recruit Top 75 quarterback Peter Bourque, who was starring in the Eagles' backyard at Marion (Mass.) Tabor Academy, highlighted its disconnect with the top Power Four talent-producing program in New England.That the Eagles' indoor practice facility is named after a Tabor graduate only added to the situation but the relationship is in the mending process as evidenced by Boston College getting a commitment from Tabor offensive lineman Dominic Maser in mid June. Two weeks later class of 2028 athlete Mikey Landers of Tabor committed to the Eagles."I think Dominic and Mikey are really good fits for Boston College," Tabor coach Jeff Moore. "We are very excited that they are going there."Moore is no stranger to Boston College, and has long been a proponent of having his players look hard at the program. In fact, when class of 2026 standout and Top 100 edge rusher Carter Gooden was going through the process, he visited Boston College more than any other program but eventually signed with Tennessee."I think we have kids that want to be good in everything they do," said Moore, who had spring conversations with Boston College coach Bill O'Brien. "So when there are schools that play in one of the best conferences in the country that has incredibly high academic standards, it's very advantageous for our kids to heavily consider schools like that."Moore knows the value of Boston College's degree, and its football capabilities. He grew up in Massachusetts, had assistant coaching stints at Yale and UMass, and was the head coach at Oakdale (Conn.) St. Thomas More and Windsor (Conn.) Loomis Chaffee before he arrived at Tabor.  He sent linebacker Edwin Kolenge to Boston College in the 2022 class, which was Moore's last season at Loomis Chaffee."Being committed to Boston College means a lot to me," Maser told 247Sports when he made his decision." It's a historic ACC program that me and my family know very well due to my grandfather coaching back in the 1980s. It also means a lot because it was my first visit back in 2023 when I was a 180-pound freshman, and now it's my last visit. So that's something I think is special since it came full circle."The rub with Tabor and Boston College centered on Bourque, according to sources. He began his high school career playing for coach John DiBiaso at West Roxbury (Mass.) Catholic Memorial but he transferred to Tabor before the 2024 season. Boston College's quarterbacks coach is Jonathan DiBiaso, who is the son of the Catholic Memorial coach. He also was recruiting Tabor.After Bourque transferred to Tabor, Boston College cut off communication. When general manager Kenyatta Watson arrived at Boston College last offseason, he worked to repair the relationship and even set up Bourque for a spring visit only to have the Eagles cancel it the day before it was to take place.The frosty relationship began to thaw in the spring, which is when Boston College changed its recruiting coverage map. Linebackers coach Dan O'Brien, who played at Boston College and is the son of former  Eagles head coach Tom O'Brien, now recruits the Massachusetts prep schools, which includes Tabor.Tabor  is where John Fish prepped and played football. Boston College's indoor practice facility is the Fish Field House. Further illustrating Boston College's desire to recruit Tabor is assistant general manager Julian Rowe-Cohen and O'Brien attended Tabor's spring showcase, and they spoke with Moore and some of the prospects. The lines of communication remain open. Watson also made recruiting the school a priority, and he is in regular contact with the staff."I think a lot of our kids would be very interested in being able to play Power Four football close to home," Moore said.There will be plenty of opportunities for Boston College to recruit Tabor, which had three players in the 2026 class sign with Power Four programs, have four in the 2027 class committed to Power Four programs and have four class of 2028 prospects with Power Four offers on the roster, including Catholic Memorial transfer linebacker Liam Conlon and defensive lineman Simon Nuamah. Both are Top247 prospects with Boston College offers.

titleText: The latest intel on 2028 QB Brady Quinn: Standouts, fall visit plans and decision timeline
mainText: The state of Florida's top two ranked quarterbacks are already committed. Bradenton (Fla.) IMG Academy signal caller Jayden Wade is committed to Georgia while Plantation (Fla.) American Heritage quarterback Neimann Lawrence pledged to Texas last month.Fort Lauderdale (Fla.) Chaminade Madonna three-star quarterback Brady Quinn is in that next tier of quarterbacks still uncommitted in the Sunshine State. As a junior, Quinn is expected to lead a loaded offensive unit for Chaminade, the school that produced Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith.His recruitment already features plenty of Power Four interest -- but things could ramp up further during and after this upcoming season. Quinn spoke with 247Sports to provide the very latest in his recruitment.

titleText: Jaiden Fields commits: Why Oklahoma was 'the place' for coveted DB
mainText: Back in June of 2025, Jaiden Fields was leaving Oklahoma with a brand new offer. And at that time, he started to realize he might want to pledge to the Sooners one day.Just over a year later, Fields is officially an OU commit. A long and winding road leads to a rewarding end result."I would say it's been a roller coaster," Fields said about his recruitment."When I got the (OU) offer at first, I was thinking 'Oh yeah, this is the place'," Fields continued. "I felt it."Oklahoma was always seen as an attractive landing spot, but the path to Norman for Fields was far from clearcut."I didn't hear from them for awhile there," Fields said. "So it was like, dang. And I kind of moved on."Time passed, Fields and Oklahoma both continued to navigate the cycle.But once it became clear OU wanted to bring Fields to Norman, credit to OU wide receivers coach Emmett Jones for kickstarting the process."Coach Jones came back and offered me at receiver," Fields said. "That's what really got me back into seeing what OU was talking about. Then Coach Hall and Coach Nagy came in and said I'm going to play defense for them. And from there, they started ramping up the recruitment for me on that side of the ball."Oklahoma safeties coach Brandon Hall and general manager Jim Nagy stepped in once the Sooners agreed to target Fields as a safety. Taking OU's pursuit up to a completely new level, the effort from these two is what elevated Oklahoma in the end."They've had a very big impact," Fields said. "Coach Hall, Coach Venables offered me back at the camp... After not hearing from them, them coming back and pushing hard to get me to commit there was big. It's been great since I reconnected with them."The development of these relationships, plus a strong pitch from the Oklahoma staff, helped Fields feel best about OU's ability to push him towards the best version of himself."Brent Venables has the blueprint," Fields said. "He's put so many players in the league. From when he was at Clemson, when he was at OU both times, other places... He puts guys in the NFL everywhere he goes.""And then, Jim Nagy, he's been in the league and he's worked in college," Fields added. "He knows what NFL talent looks like, and he says I have that."Fields has always wanted to play at the highest levels of football. While he wasn't always exactly sure what the process looked like to get there, he dedicated himself to making it happen. Fields turns a dream into reality, and he couldn't be more thrilled his efforts led him to Oklahoma. He now looks forward to making an impact in Norman."It all means a lot," Fields said. "When I was younger, sure, I wanted to go to the NFL. But I didn't think about college, I'd never really thought about it. Once I started playing, and I got my first offer, it hit me that I can really do this. It hit me that I can get offers, I really have a chance, I might even be able to go to the league. It wows me every time. Just thinking about the past, how I was and where I wanted to go... Now that I have a chance to actually go out there and do that, it's so special to me."***GET ALL THINGS OKLAHOMA STRAIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL INBOX FOR FREE -- SIGN UP FOR THE SOONERS ILLUSTRATED NEWSLETTER TODAY***Fields chooses Oklahoma over SMU, Texas A&M, TCU and Stanford.The Hutto (Texas) High star rates as a top-50 athlete nationally in 247Sports' rankings. Fields is also seen as the No. 89 prospect inside the talented Lone Star State.Fields joins a safety haul for the Sooners that includes Bode Sparrow and Jaylen Scott. An impressive trio part of a strong 2027 class for Oklahoma.

titleText: ASU surges for fast-rising OL Manase Brown: "They are my No. 1 spot right now"
mainText: The first official visit is always an eye-opening one for recruits, particularly for those that didn't get to hit the road consistently.Fast-rising offensive tackle Manase Brown is among that group.Arizona State was first up and, although the three-star lineman from Draper (Utah) Corner Canyon has a couple more stops planned on his recruiting journey ahead of what a scheduled summertime commitment, it's emphatically setting the benchmark."Everything at ASU feels like home and feels natural," Brown told 247Sports. "They are my No. 1 spot right now of where I want to be."The players' thoughts on the school and on the coaches really was a highlight for me. It's a strong brotherhood and you can feel it on campus as soon as you land."Brown just recently made the full-time switch to offensive tackle after starring at edge rusher and tight end through his first three seasons of varsity football. He was previously rated No. 89 nationally among edges, and his highly intriguing 6-foot-7, 260-pound frame drew significant interest from college programs throughout the spring evaluation period.Hometown suitor BYU (June 19) also has an official visit on the calendar. (Photo: Blair Angulo, 247Sports)Brown originally planned to make a decision during the season, particularly because of his new position and the possibility that new programs could get involved after seeing the first few games of his senior year on film.Yet after seeing things up close, the Sun Devils have ramped up pursuit and Brown said he's actually planning to make a decision sooner rather than later."I love their offensive scheme," Brown said. "It is very well balanced. It's great at both running the ball and passing it."The best pitch they made for me, really, was that they're not trying to sell anything to you. It was genuine. There is no fake. No BS. It's all real talk, and if someone wants to come here, great. Either way, they aren't going to change the way they operate and how they add players to the roster."ASU already holds a very prominent commitment at offensive tackle in the 2027 cycle from four-star Jake Hildebrand, the No. 1-rated prospect in the Grand Canyon State.Despite having only eight commitments so far in the class the Sun Devils rank No. 8 among Big 12 programs in the 247Sports Composite team recruiting rankings.Stay tuned to 247Sports for breaking news, insight and analysis as prospects across all classes continue to sort through their top contenders.
